_meta.note: Simplified orbit model. Numbers are plausible, not flight-qualified.

fields.revisit_hours: time between two passes over the same target, single satellite
fields.comm_window_pct: percent of each orbit with a usable ground link
fields.downlink_mbps: raw downlink rate when in a comm window
fields.radiation_index: 0-1 relative dose; high values need rad-hard parts (+cost)
fields.base_lifetime_years: propellant-limited lifetime before station-keeping runs out
fields.cost_multiplier: applies to the bus cost (harder environment = pricier parts)

orbits.name: LEO Sun-Synchronous 400 km
orbits.blurb: Constant lighting angle — the standard imaging orbit.
orbits.tradeoff: Only 24% of the orbit has a ground link, and atmospheric drag limits lifetime.

orbits.name: LEO 550 km (mid-inclination)
orbits.blurb: Better comm coverage over populated latitudes, faster revisit.
orbits.tradeoff: Inconsistent sun angle — harder to compare images over time.

orbits.name: MEO 20,200 km
orbits.blurb: Wide coverage, long life, lots of comm time.
orbits.tradeoff: Terrible revisit for a single satellite, and radiation forces expensive parts.

orbits.name: GEO 35,786 km
orbits.blurb: Sits still over one spot: ideal for comms and continuous weather watching.
orbits.tradeoff: Too far for any small imager to see detail — resolution penalty is severe.
